#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_install_pin.sh — SEC-07 (#795) pin-integrity gate for the vpinned
# release-marker model.
#
# The installer's default does NOT carry a baked-in version: it resolves
# the `vpinned` release marker (a GitHub Release whose PINNED_VERSION asset
# names the current known-good release). That removes the #1015 failure
# class (a committed pin rotting) — and this gate guards the marker:
#
#   1. E_PIN_DRIFT — the generated site/install.sh must track the vpinned
#      marker and embed a trust anchor identical to the config's
#      signing_public_key.
#   2. E_PIN_MISSING / E_PIN_INVALID — the marker release must publish a
#      well-formed PINNED_VERSION (a vX.Y.Z-ish tag).
#   3. E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING / E_PIN_PROVENANCE_INVALID — the MARKED
#      release must publish SHA256SUMS + a signature that verifies against
#      the committed trust anchor (the marker itself is never trusted —
#      this is what makes a tampered pointer fail closed).
#   4. E_PIN_ASSET_COVERAGE — the signed manifest must cover every
#      platform archive the installer can request.
#
# Modes:
#   (default)   full gate: drift checks + marker + marked-release provenance
#   --offline   drift checks only (no network)
#
# FA_PIN_TARGET=<tag> verifies a concrete tag instead of following the
# marker — pin_release.sh uses this to prove a NEW release BEFORE pointing
# the marker at it.
#
# Overridable inputs (tests/fixtures):
#   FA_PIN_CONFIG        install-config.yaml path (default: site/install-config.yaml)
#   FA_PIN_INSTALLER     generated install.sh path (default: site/install.sh)
#   FA_PIN_RELEASE_BASE  release download base (default:
#                        https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/download)
#
# Exit 0 with "ok" lines on success; exit 1 with an E_PIN_* line on failure
# (the selftest greps for these markers).
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CONFIG="${FA_PIN_CONFIG:-$REPO_ROOT/site/install-config.yaml}"
INSTALLER="${FA_PIN_INSTALLER:-$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh}"
RELEASE_BASE="${FA_PIN_RELEASE_BASE:-https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/download}"
TARGET_OVERRIDE="${FA_PIN_TARGET:-}"
OFFLINE=false
[ "${1:-}" = "--offline" ] && OFFLINE=true

err() { printf '✘ %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()  { printf 'ok  %s\n' "$*"; }

# Every archive site/install.sh can request — the signed manifest must
# cover all of them, or some platform installs unverifiable.
REQUIRED_ASSETS="fa-linux-x64.tar.gz fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz fa-macos-arm64.tar.gz fa-macos-x64.tar.gz fa-windows-x64.zip"

fetch() { # fetch <url> <out>
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -fsSL "$1" -o "$2"
  else
    wget -qO "$2" "$1"
  fi
}

# ── 1. drift: generated installer tracks the marker; anchors match ─────────
[ -f "$CONFIG" ] || err "E_PIN_CONFIG: install config not found: $CONFIG"
[ -f "$INSTALLER" ] || err "E_PIN_DRIFT: generated installer not found: $INSTALLER"
grep -q 'FA_VERSION="${FA_VERSION:-vpinned}"' "$INSTALLER" \
  || err "E_PIN_DRIFT: $INSTALLER does not default to the vpinned marker — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart), never hand-edit generated files"
work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$CONFIG" | sed 's/^ *//' > "$work/config-anchor.pem"
grep -q "BEGIN PUBLIC KEY" "$work/config-anchor.pem" \
  || err "E_PIN_CONFIG: no signing_public_key block in $CONFIG"
openssl pkey -pubin -in "$work/config-anchor.pem" -noout 2>/dev/null \
  || err "E_PIN_CONFIG: signing_public_key in $CONFIG does not parse as a public key"
sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$INSTALLER" \
  | sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > "$work/installer-anchor.pem"
cmp "$work/config-anchor.pem" "$work/installer-anchor.pem" \
  || err "E_PIN_DRIFT: the trust anchor embedded in $INSTALLER differs from install.signing_public_key in $CONFIG — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"
ok "(1) no drift: installer tracks the vpinned marker; trust anchors match"

$OFFLINE && { ok "(offline) drift checks only — marker/provenance skipped"; exit 0; }

# ── 2. resolve the target: marker (default) or FA_PIN_TARGET override ──────
if [ -n "$TARGET_OVERRIDE" ]; then
  case "$TARGET_OVERRIDE" in
    v*) vtag="$TARGET_OVERRIDE" ;;
    *)  vtag="v$TARGET_OVERRIDE" ;;
  esac
  ok "(2) target override: $vtag (marker not consulted)"
else
  if ! fetch "$RELEASE_BASE/vpinned/PINNED_VERSION" "$work/PINNED_VERSION"; then
    err "E_PIN_MISSING: the vpinned marker publishes no PINNED_VERSION at $RELEASE_BASE/vpinned/PINNED_VERSION — create the marker release (scripts/pin_release.sh) before serving this installer"
  fi
  resolved="$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$work/PINNED_VERSION")"
  case "$resolved" in
    ''|*[!0-9A-Za-z.-]*) err "E_PIN_INVALID: the vpinned marker returned '$resolved' — not a release tag" ;;
  esac
  case "$resolved" in
    v*) vtag="$resolved" ;;
    *)  vtag="v$resolved" ;;
  esac
  ok "(2) marker resolves to: $vtag"
fi

# ── 3. the marked release must carry signed provenance ──────────────────────
sums_url="$RELEASE_BASE/$vtag/SHA256SUMS"
sig_url="$RELEASE_BASE/$vtag/SHA256SUMS.sig"
fetch "$sums_url" "$work/SHA256SUMS" \
  || err "E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING: release $vtag publishes no SHA256SUMS at $sums_url — the marker must not point at an unsigned release (or assets are still uploading; retry)"
fetch "$sig_url" "$work/SHA256SUMS.sig" \
  || err "E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING: release $vtag publishes no SHA256SUMS.sig at $sig_url — refusing a pin without provenance"
ok "(3) release $vtag publishes SHA256SUMS + signature"

# ── 4. signature must verify against the committed trust anchor ─────────────
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify "$work/config-anchor.pem" \
  -signature "$work/SHA256SUMS.sig" "$work/SHA256SUMS" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || err "E_PIN_PROVENANCE_INVALID: SHA256SUMS.sig on release $vtag does not verify against the trust anchor in $CONFIG — possible drift or tampering"
ok "(4) signature verifies against the committed trust anchor"

# ── 5. the signed manifest must cover every installable platform archive ────
missing=""
for a in $REQUIRED_ASSETS; do
  grep -q "  $a\$" "$work/SHA256SUMS" || missing="$missing $a"
done
[ -z "$missing" ] \
  || err "E_PIN_ASSET_COVERAGE: signed SHA256SUMS on release $vtag does not cover:$missing — every platform archive must be checksummed by the signed manifest"
ok "(5) signed manifest covers all platform archives"

echo ""
echo "check_install_pin: target '$vtag' satisfies the provenance gate"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pin_release.sh — advance the `vpinned` release marker to a freshly signed
# tag. PURE RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION: no commits, no pushes, no
# working-tree mutation — the marker lives entirely in GitHub Releases.
# The tag-scoped install-pin-bump CI job runs this after release-provenance
# published SHA256SUMS(.sig) for the tag.
#
# Trust model (SEC-07 #795): the marker is only a POINTER. Before it moves,
# the target release must pass check_install_pin.sh (signature verifies
# against the committed trust anchor + full platform coverage); after it
# moves, the gate runs again against the marker itself. A compromised
# marker therefore degrades to a DoS (install fails closed), never to a
# bad binary — the installer's embedded anchor is the real trust root.
#
# Usage:
#   pin_release.sh <tag>            point the vpinned marker at <tag> (vX.Y.Z)
#   pin_release.sh is-newer <a> <b> exit 0 iff semver(a) > semver(b)
#                                   (v-prefixes stripped; numeric compare)
#
# Environment:
#   GH_TOKEN             release write token (live mode)
#   PIN_RELEASE_BASE     file:// dir acting as the release root — fixture
#                        mode: the marker becomes $base/vpinned/PINNED_VERSION
#                        and no gh/network is touched (selftest/dry runs)
#   PIN_RELEASE_REPO     owner/repo for gh calls (default: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness)
#   MARKER_TAG           marker release/tag name (default: vpinned)
# POSIX-only below: Ubuntu's /bin/sh is dash — no pipefail, no arrays/[[]].
# Enable pipefail only where the shell supports it (same convention as
# site/install.sh.template).
set -eu
( set -o pipefail ) 2>/dev/null && set -o pipefail || true

MARKER="${MARKER_TAG:-vpinned}"
REPO="${PIN_RELEASE_REPO:-IstiN/flutter_agent_harness}"
BASE="${PIN_RELEASE_BASE:-https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download}"

# ── is-newer <a> <b>: numeric semver compare, v-prefix tolerated ────────────
# POSIX-pure on purpose: ubuntu runners give `sh` = dash and `awk` = mawk,
# whose printf does not apply the %010d zero-padding this compare relies on
# (the old awk ver_key made equal keys and silently reported "not newer").
# Here every component is normalized with the SHELL printf (dash/bash both
# implement %010d) to a zero-padded digit string — pure digits of equal
# length, so the lexical `>` is collation-independent.
if [ "${1:-}" = "is-newer" ]; then
  a="$(printf '%s' "${2:?usage: is-newer <a> <b>}" | sed 's/^v//')"
  b="$(printf '%s' "${3:?usage: is-newer <a> <b>}" | sed 's/^v//')"
  a_num="${a%%-*}"; a_sfx="${a#"$a_num"}"
  b_num="${b%%-*}"; b_sfx="${b#"$b_num"}"
  # leading digits of a dotted component, zero-stripped, padded to 10
  comp10() {
    c="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -cd '0-9' | sed -e 's/^0*//' -e 's/^$/0/')"
    printf '%010d' "$c"
  }
  split3() { # $1 = "X.Y.Z" → newline-separated X, Y, Z (missing pieces empty)
    rest="$1"
    c1="${rest%%.*}"; [ "$c1" = "$rest" ] && rest="" || rest="${rest#*.}"
    c2="${rest%%.*}"; [ "$c2" = "$rest" ] && c3="" || c3="${rest#*.}"
    printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$c1" "$c2" "$c3"
  }
  # sed-extract instead of `set -- $(...)` — word-splitting drops the empty
  # components, and `set -u` then kills $2/$3 in dash.
  a123="$(split3 "$a_num")"
  a1="$(printf '%s\n' "$a123" | sed -n 1p)"
  a2="$(printf '%s\n' "$a123" | sed -n 2p)"
  a3="$(printf '%s\n' "$a123" | sed -n 3p)"
  b123="$(split3 "$b_num")"
  b1="$(printf '%s\n' "$b123" | sed -n 1p)"
  b2="$(printf '%s\n' "$b123" | sed -n 2p)"
  b3="$(printf '%s\n' "$b123" | sed -n 3p)"
  ka="$(comp10 "$a1")$(comp10 "$a2")$(comp10 "$a3")"
  kb="$(comp10 "$b1")$(comp10 "$b2")$(comp10 "$b3")"
  if [ "$ka" != "$kb" ]; then
    [ "$ka" \> "$kb" ]
    exit $?
  fi
  # equal numerics: a release outranks its own pre-release; release vs
  # release is equal (NOT newer)
  if [ -z "$a_sfx" ] && [ -n "$b_sfx" ]; then exit 0; fi
  if [ -n "$a_sfx" ] || [ -z "$b_sfx" ]; then exit 1; fi
  [ "$a_sfx" \> "$b_sfx" ]
  exit $?
fi

tag="${1:?usage: pin_release.sh <vX.Y.Z>}"
case "$tag" in
  v*) version="${tag#v}" ;;
  *)  version="$tag"; tag="v$tag" ;;
esac
echo "pin_release: target $tag (marker: $MARKER)"

# The gate speaks URLs; a bare fixture path gets a file:// scheme. The raw
# path is kept for fixture-mode marker writes.
BASE_URL="$BASE"
case "$BASE_URL" in
  *://*) ;;
  *) BASE_URL="file://$BASE_URL" ;;
esac

fetch_text() {
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then curl -fsSL "$1"; else wget -qO- "$1"; fi
}

# ── 1. read the current marker (absent = first pin) ─────────────────────────
current=""
if current="$(fetch_text "$BASE_URL/$MARKER/PINNED_VERSION" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')"; then
  echo "pin_release: marker currently at $current"
else
  echo "pin_release: no marker yet — first pin"
fi
if [ -n "$current" ] && ! "$0" is-newer "$version" "$current"; then
  echo "pin_release: marker is already at $current (>= $tag) — nothing to do."
  exit 0
fi

# ── 2. the target must pass the provenance gate BEFORE the marker moves ─────
# FA_PIN_TARGET checks the concrete tag regardless of where the marker

# window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays out — baselines are macOS-captured;

binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own GREEN push run IS
    # the gate (the dedupe lookup fires only on conclusion == "success") —
    # the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac binary built under Rosetta on the self-hosted macos-m5 pool
          # (no GitHub-hosted macOS runners in this repo).
          - runner: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh, whose
          # conventional-commit fallback reads commit MESSAGES since the
          # previous tag — same reason release-macos fetches full
          # (gh-1477: blobless, never historical file blobs). Whichever
          # matrix leg wins the create race must be able to produce the
          # full curated body.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          # gh-2120: PINNED — the unpinned stable float (3.13.5 -> 3.14.0 on
          # 2026-11-11) changed `dart build cli`'s output layout mid-stream
          # (self-contained bin/fa -> thin dartaotruntime-style binary +
          # lib/libdartaotfah.so); the published v1.0.709 bundle broke every
          # machine-loop fa launch (dartaotruntime: "not an AOT snapshot",
          # exit 255 at agent startup). Same exact-patch policy build-macos.yml
          # already applies to its flutter-version pins. Bump deliberately,
          # in the commit that verifies the new layout end-to-end.

{
            echo '## fa-extension.zip NOT shipped this release'
            echo ''
            echo 'The extension build job failed (continue-on-error: the gh-1832 gate strands the release without it). See the failed steps above.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # SEC-07 (#795): the installer's default trust path is SIGNED checksums.
  # This job aggregates every fa-* asset of the release into SHA256SUMS and
  # signs it with the FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY repo secret (openssl RSA —
  # already available on runners, no new dependency). The signing key is a
  # channel separate from the release assets, so a checksum file served from
  # the same compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself.
  # Fail-closed: without the secret the release publishes NO provenance and
  # this job goes red — install.sh aborts with E_PROVENANCE_MISSING on it.
  # Needs web-spa (#1100, continue-on-error) and build-extension
  # (gh-1847, continue-on-error) for ordering only: the web bundle and
  # the extension zip cannot hold CLI provenance hostage. The ordering
  # makes the fa-* sweep deterministic — web-spa/extension success ->
  # zip signed, failure -> zip absent — never a half-updated manifest,
  # and the gh-1832 gate below never races a slow attach.
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          #
          # gh-2042 (BLOCKING review thread): the flip must never drag the
          # `latest` badge backwards. The drift remediation
          # (scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh) re-requests THIS job for
          # an old drifted tag; a job rerun re-executes this step with the
          # original run's ref, and an unconditional --latest would
          # re-flag that older release as Latest — pointing every
          # `fa update` client DOWN at it (the re-signed manifest would
          # make the downgrade pass provenance). Carry --latest ONLY when
          # the release is still a draft (the normal publish point,
          # gh-1801) or already the current latest; otherwise publish the
          # re-signed state without touching the badge.
          is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
          current_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$current_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          else
            # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is
            # already correct — never drag the latest badge backwards
            # (gh-2042).
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          fi

      # gh-1899: the flip above publishes exactly ONE release object, but
      # GitHub does not atomically enforce one release per tag — two train
      # legs racing the lazy draft create can BOTH succeed (v1.0.641, run
      # 40163369302: twin drafts 87 ms apart), and the unpicked twin then
      # rots until the 24h sweeper deletes it and files a recurring sweep
      # issue. The tag is published and servable now: reclaim this run's
      # twin drafts. Success-path only — a red provenance keeps the draft
      # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel.
      # Best-effort by design (gh-1899 review): the flip above already
      # published the release — a cleanup-only API blip here must NOT fail
      # the provenance job (release-asset-smoke gates on its result and
      # would silently skip for a release that is actually fine). Warn
      # and stay green; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop.
      - name: Reclaim orphaned draft twins (gh-1899)
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"

  # Train-level draft lifecycle guard (issue #282, gh-2230): this train is
  # the PUBLISH OWNER of every staged draft (gh-1801 rework —
  # release-provenance above is the sole --draft=false --latest flip), but

# staged draft: the creating run's jobs all succeeded (their guards never
  # fire), the failed train is superseded and never rerun, and
  # verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only — so the draft rotted
  # exactly 24h until the daily sweeper deleted it and filed the recurring
  # sweep issue (gh-2230, v1.0.728). This job runs AFTER the publish point
  # settled — needs release-provenance + always(), so it fires on failed AND
  # cancelled trains and never on the success path's result (the script
  # no-ops on a published release). The script deletes ONLY when the
  # publish point is unreachable (result == 'skipped' — rerun --failed
  # never resurrects skipped jobs): drafts for THIS train's tag whose
  # owner-marker run has completed (scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh).
  # A failed/cancelled provenance is rerunnable, so the staged draft stays
  # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention). In-flight
  # owner runs and unmarked/human drafts stay with the sweeper (E1).
  train-draft-guard:
    name: Train draft lifecycle guard
    needs: release-provenance
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    if: >-
      always() &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete the orphaned staged draft (issue #282 E2)
      actions: read # probe the draft-owner marker run's status (gh-2008 pattern)
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Delete drafts the failed train will never publish
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PROVENANCE_RESULT: ${{ needs.release-provenance.result }}
        run: bash scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

Very important: the `train-draft-guard` job ran AFTER release-provenance with always(). The script deletes the staged draft ONLY when the publish point (provenance) is unreachable (result == 'skipped') AND the owner run has completed. Wait — did train-draft-guard run in our failed run? Looking at the failed run's job list... I saw "Release pending check", "Release dedupe check", "Classify changes"... I didn't see "Train draft lifecycle guard" in the listing output (it was truncated — grep filtered only X/- lines plus some). The annotation in the macos job was from `release_draft_guard.sh` (per-creating-job guard) — different script (release_draft_guard vs release_train_draft_guard).

WAIT — the train-draft-guard script "deletes ONLY when the publish point is unreachable (result == 'skipped' — rerun --failed never resurrects skipped jobs): drafts for THIS train's tag whose owner-marker run has completed". In our case provenance result == 'skipped'! So the train-draft-guard SHOULD have deleted the v1.0.782 draft... but the draft still exists (created 13:32:24). Why? Conditions: (a) draft owner marker = run/45830131519/job/binaries-windows-x64; owner run completed (cancelled at 15:42). Hmm — "owner-marker run has completed" — the run WAS completed at the time train-draft-guard ran? The train-draft-guard job itself is part of the same run — it runs while the run is still in_progress (it's a job OF the run!). The guard ran at ~15:41-15:42 (after macos was cancelled at 15:41:39 and pin-bump at 15:41:50). At that moment the run was still in_progress — the owner-marker run hasn't completed (IT IS the current run). So the guard correctly left the draft ("In-flight owner runs ... stay with the sweper (E1)").

OK so now the design intent is fully clear:
- A cancelled/skipped-publish train leaves the draft to the 24h sweper OR to a manual rerun.
- The repo treats "rerun --failed never resurrects skipped jobs" as a first-class constraint and builds cascades around it (install-pin-bump always(); train-draft-guard deleting only-skipped drafts).

Now the recovery path for v1.0.782 TODAY (before the 24h sweper at ~13:32 tomorrow deletes the draft):
- Full rerun of run 45830131519 (attempt 2): all jobs re-run. binaries-macos-x64 re-runs — IF fa-m5-3 git fetch works, uploads fa-macos-x64.tar.gz to... wait, the draft already exists (owned by binaries-windows-x64); the rerun's windows leg would hit the draft-owner guard: "refusing to delete a draft this run+job did not create" — but does it refuse to UPLOAD too? The guard is about DELETING a draft another job created. Uploading attaches assets regardless. The lazy-create script (release_draft_guard.sh) refuses DELETE only. Upload should proceed. Then provenance (attempt 2: binaries result success) → download fa-* (all 6 platform archives + extension + web-spa) → gate passes → sign → flip → publish. Then install-pin-bump → marker advances → smoke → green.

- OR rerun-failed: resurrects cancelled macos leg + failed pin-bump only; provenance stays skipped → pin-bump fails again. NOT sufficient. (And the run-level conclusion would remain red.)

So: **full rerun is the required recovery action**.

"Golden suite (macOS baselines)" and "Cube kernel live (macOS)" ran in the v1.0.782 run — on self-hosted? Let me check whether any later run exercised fa-m5-3 successfully.

and no guard fails CI).
- **Train-level draft lifecycle guard** (gh-2230) — the per-job guards
  above fire only on their own job's failure, but since the gh-1801
  rework the staged draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN (ci.yml's
  `release-provenance`, the sole publish point). A train that dies
  upstream of the publish point (core tests → quality-gate red → binaries
  skipped → provenance skipped) used to orphan the staged draft until the
  24h sweeper reclaimed it and filed the recurring sweep issue. ci.yml now
  carries a `train-draft-guard` job (`needs: release-provenance`,
  `if: always()` on tag-push/release events) running
  `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh` with the publish point's settled
  result exported. It deletes ONLY when that result is `skipped` (the
  publish point is unreachable — `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped
  jobs): drafts for the trained tag whose well-formed ownership marker
  names a COMPLETED run go away (a superseded failed train is never rerun,
  so nobody else would ever publish them; the git tag is untouched). A
  FAILED or CANCELLED provenance is rerunnable, so the staged draft stays
  as the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention). Fail-safe
  keeps — in-flight owner runs (a concurrent creator leg may be
  mid-upload), unmarked/human drafts (E1), any owner-status lookup failure
  (never delete blind), and an unexported result; the sweeper remains the
  backstop. Grants `contents: write` + `actions: read`, same
  stub-enforced model as the sweep-drafts job.
- **Attach-or-create** — the draft-capable creates of build-macos.yml /
  build-mobile.yml live in `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`, which is
  idempotent under the view→create race (#282 E3): a create that loses to
  a concurrent winner uploads into the winner's release instead of
  failing (a failing create would fire the guard against the winner's
  in-flight draft), and the create stamps the ownership marker the guard
  verifies.
- **Twin-draft self-dedupe** (gh-2372) — the view→create race above is
  NOT benign for drafts: GitHub does not enforce one release per tag for
  DRAFT objects, so two sibling legs of one run racing the window
  (production: the same second — v1.0.760's build-macos-cli twin vs its
  published build-extension sibling; v1.0.763's build-extension twin)
  BOTH create successfully. The train publishes exactly one; the twin
  rots 24h+ and re-files the recurring sweep issue with the misleading
  "a `gh release create` step died" prose (nothing died — every creating
  job succeeded, and `release_draft_dedupe.sh` matches only the TRAIN's
  own-run twins, so child-run twins were invisible to every guard). After
  a successful draft create, `release_lazy_draft.sh` and
  `release_attach_or_create.sh` now run
  `scripts/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh <tag>`: when an OLDER (lower id =
  first-created) same-tag release exists that is published or
  pipeline-created (well-formed marker / Bot author / machine account),
  every draft carrying THIS job's exact ownership marker is deleted by id
  and the caller attaches into the winner by tag — on the
  `release_attach_or_create.sh` path the create CARRIED the assets, so a
  lost election falls through to the E3 attach block in the SAME run (a
  body-marker probe tells our surviving draft from the winner; the
  winner path re-uploads nothing), while `release_lazy_draft.sh`'s loser
  is asset-free and the train's attach steps upload by tag — the
  deterministic election makes the gh-1801 tolerance contract ("the
  loser uploads into the winner's release") actually true. Human
  (unmarked) drafts never win
  and are never touched (E1); the script is best-effort (warn + green —
  the sweeper is the backstop) except for a malformed identity, which
  fails loud like the marker-stamping scripts. Pinned by

content.thinking:
This documentation is extremely relevant. Key finding: the repo's own gh-2318 early reclaim and gh-2230 train-draft-guard embody the invariant: **"A FAILED or CANCELED provenance is rerunnable → rerun --failed recovery vessel; a SKIPPED provenance is unreachable → nobody will ever publish it"**.

In our v1.0.782 case: provenance is SKIPPED → the whole train is unrecoverable via rerun-failed. The docs explicitly say for this state the recovery is... hmm, for pub.dev: "re-run the failed ci.yml tag-publish run (a rerun keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)" — i.e. a FULL rerun.

Now — the decision on what the FIX for this bug ticket should be. Let me enumerate what went wrong and what's actionable in-repo:

**Failure chain:**
1. fa-m5-3 (self-hosted macOS runner) hung 45 min inside `git fetch --filter=blob:none --unshallow` during checkout of the macos-x64 binaries leg.
2. `timeout-minutes: 45` fired → the leg was cancelled ("The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 45m0s").
3. `binaries` job result = cancelled → `release-provenance` SKIPPED (its if requires binaries.result == 'success').
4. Release stayed a draft (missing fa-macos-x64.tar.gz, SHA256SUMS, .sig); previous release v1.0.781 stayed latest; marker stayed at v1.0.781 (fail-closed — CORECT).
5. `install-pin-bump` (always()) ran and failed loud with E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING — correct per design.
6. The run is red; the ticket `[ci-red] v1.0.782 failed` was filed (Failed jobs: Advance vpinned marker).

**The gap (the actual bug worth fixing in-repo):** When `binaries` settles CANCELED or FAILED on a release train, `release-provenance` SKIPS. Per the repo's own invariant, a skipped publish point is UNRECOVERABLE via `rerun --failed` (the documented recovery path), the draft rots to the 24h sweper, the tag stays red forever, and the vpinned marker stays stale until manual full-rerun. The v1.0.483 precedent fixed exactly this pattern for `install-pin-bump` by making it run-and-fail-loud instead of skip ("a FAILED job IS part of rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it"). `release-provenance` never got the same treatment — even though it is the publish point and its gh-1832 required-assets gate already fails closed BEFORE signing or publishing (safe to run with missing assets).

So the targeted fix: change `release-provenance.if` from
`!cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' && (tag gate)`
to
`!cancelled() && needs.binaries.result != 'skipped' && (tag gate)`

i.e. the provenance job RUNS whenever the train reached the binaries stage (success/canceled/failure), letting the gh-1832 gate fail loud on missing assets, keeping the run rerunnable to green. When binaries SKIPS (gate failed upstream / non-release ref), provenance still skips (nothing was built; nothing to sign — and the train-draft-guard/sweper handle draft hygiene for that state... wait, no draft exists in that state since binaries creates drafts lazily... except web-spa/build-extension continue-on-error legs may create drafts? Let me check: web-spa and build-extension are `needs` of provenance with continue-on-error ordering. Do THEY create drafts? The gh-189 text mentions build-extension attaching to the release... and "the extension zip cannot hold CLI provenance hostage". If binaries skips but web-spa ran (continue-on-error), could there be a draft with web assets? In the gate-failed state, do web-spa/build-extension run? They'd be gated on the same tag push event... let me check their if conditions. If binaries skipped (gate failed), web-spa likely also skipped (gated on release-pending == true && event is tag push). Hmm — release-pending/dedupe: on tag push, pending should be true. quality-gate fails → binaries skipped; web-spa: needs? Let me check web-spa/build-extension if conditions to make sure `!= 'skipped'` is exactly right for them too. Also important: the provenance steps themselves: "Collect release assets" downloads fa-* — if the DRAFT doesn't exist at all (binaries skipped case — no draft), `gh release download` FAILS → loud. But we skip in that case anyway.

Edge case: what if binaries.result == 'failure' because ONE leg failed (compile error)? provenance runs → collect fa-* succeeds (partial set from draft) → gh-1832 gate FAILS (missing the failed leg's asset) → loud, draft preserved, rerunnable. When the compile error is FIXED (new tag), fine. When someone reruns the failed windows leg, provenance re-runs → publishes. GOOD.

Edge case: binaries.result == 'cancelled' from a TIMEOUT (our case): provenance runs → gate fails (missing asset) → loud + rerunnable. GOOD.

Now the second question: does anything else DEPEND on provenance being skipped in these states? Let me grep for `release-provenance.result` consumers:
1. release-asset-smoke: `needs.release-provenance.result == 'success'` — fine (still only runs on success).
2. install-pin-bump: needs provenance; always(); runs pin_release.sh — its gate fails if SHA256SUMS absent. With provenance now failing loud (instead of skipping), pin-bump still runs (always) and fails on the same missing provenance — unchanged behavior for the run conclusion, but now rerunnable.
3. train-draft-guard: DELETES the draft when provenance result == 'skipped'. With the fix, provenance will be 'failure' in these states → guard does NOT delete (rerunnable vessel).   b. The provenance-skip recovery gap: rerun-failed cannot recover a skipped publish point; only a FULL rerun can. The docs/gh-2318 treat skipped-provenance trains as "nobody will ever publish it" → delete the draft. But for the vpinned marker to advance to v1.0.782 and the ref to go green, someone must do a FULL rerun (2h of CI) or the next tag train supersedes.
   
  Hmm wait — actually, let me reconsider (b). Is a full rerun the DESIGNED recovery here, or is "wait for the next release train" the designed recovery for this class? Looking at the ci-red-report leg: it files a ticket when a tag run goes red. The ticket closes "manually when the ref goes green". When provenance SKIPS (our case), pin-bump runs while the release is a draft with partial assets → guaranteed E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING. That's BY DESIGN (loud red so rerun-failed reaches it). Not a bug.

45-minute stall mid-fetch with zero bytes — classic connection black hole (no TCP RST, no timeout). Git's default has no low-speed limit... Actually git DOES have http.lowSpeedLimit unset by default → a stalled HTTP connection waits on the OS TCP timeout (which can be ~15-30+ min on macOS with keepalive off) or indefinitely on a dead-but-open connection. THIS is a known git-on-self-hosted failure mode. Fix options in-repo: set `git config http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime` for checkout... but checkout is actions/checkout — can pass `token`, not git config. # gh-2332 (the v1.0.752/753/754 class): keying on quality-gate alone went
  # stale when gh-1801 moved the artifact train AFTER the gate. Three tag
  # runs went red with quality-gate green: no draft, no release object, no
  # issue — invisible unless someone scrolled the tag-filtered Actions tab.
  # Coverage = EVERY post-gate leg that can redden a tag run, keyed on its
  # DIRECT result (fa#456: never transitive skips):
  #   artifact train  binaries → release-provenance → release-asset-smoke /
  #                   installer-smoke / install-pin-bump / train-draft-guard,
  #   publish path    integration (the #551 hard provider gate) → publish,
  #   siblings        js-ext-integration, watchdog, step-timings,
  #                   faui-coverage.
  # NOT covered, deliberately: web-spa / build-extension carry job-level
  # continue-on-error (downstream needs see SUCCESS, so they cannot redden
  # a run); release / binaries-pr / binaries-smoke-gate are schedule-,
  # dispatch- or PR-scoped (never run on tag pushes); everything upstream
  # of quality-gate rides its verdict. Pinned — with the coverage set
  # DERIVED from the live needs graph, so an un-covered future leg fails
  # the guard — by test/ci_red_report_release_legs_guard_test.dart.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate, binaries, integration, js-ext-integration, publish, watchdog, step-timings, faui-coverage, release-provenance, release-asset-smoke, installer-smoke, install-pin-bump, train-draft-guard]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      github.event_name == 'push' &&
      (
        needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.binaries.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.integration.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.js-ext-integration.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.publish.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.watchdog.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.step-timings.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.faui-coverage.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.release-provenance.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.release-asset-smoke.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.installer-smoke.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.install-pin-bump.result == 'failure' ||
        needs.train-draft-guard.result == 'failure'
      )
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \

# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Advance vpinned marker` job failed on the v1.0.782 tag run, leaving the release unpublished and the `vpinned` install marker stale at v1.0.781.

## Root cause

Exact chain (run [45830131519](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/45830131519), tag `v1.0.782` @ `667cc91`):

1. **Trigger**: the self-hosted macOS runner `fa-m5-3` (`Uladzimirs-MacBook-Pro`) hung for 45 minutes inside `actions/checkout` — specifically `git -c protocol.version=2 fetch --no-tags --prune --filter=blob:none --unshallow origin …` (log: last fetch output 14:56:30Z, "The operation was canceled." 15:41:16Z). A mid-fetch connection black hole on the self-hosted machine; ~45 min with zero bytes and no failure.
2. **Timeout**: the `binaries` job carries `timeout-minutes: 45` — annotation `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 45m0s`. The `binaries-macos-x64` matrix leg was cancelled (check-run 139975970833, conclusion `cancelled`). `fail-fast: false` kept the other four legs alive (windows/linux/linux-arm64/macos-arm64 assets attached to the draft).
3. **Skip cascade**: `release-provenance` ("Sign release checksums") is gated by `if: !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' && (tag/release event)` — with `binaries` cancelled it **skipped**, so `SHA256SUMS(.sig)` were never built and the draft release (id 459528093) was never flipped to published (`--draft=false --latest` lives only there).
4. **Fail-closed marker (correct behavior, the visible symptom)**: `install-pin-bump` runs under `always()` by design (v1.0.483 lesson), so it ran and `scripts/pin_release.sh` correctly refused to move the marker: `E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING: release v1.0.782 publishes no SHA256SUMS` — "marker NOT moved". The marker stays at v1.0.781; installers keep serving the last good release. This is the SEC-07 #795 trust model working as intended.
5. **Recovery gap (the actual defect)**: with `release-provenance` **skipped**, the documented recovery vehicle is dead: `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs (repo invariant, docs/ci.md §draft lifecycle, v1.0.483). The only recoveries are a **full ~2h rerun of the whole run** (re-running the already-green 35-40 min quality gate) or waiting for the next train. The v1.0.483 fix gave `install-pin-bump` exactly this treatment (`always()` → run and fail loud → rerunnable); `release-provenance` — the publish point itself — never got it.

**Impact**: every tag train whose `binaries` matrix leg settles `cancelled`/`failure` (self-hosted hang, timeout, one red leg) produces: red run, draft rotting until the 24h sweeper, stale `vpinned` marker, and a ci-red ticket whose only remediation is a full rerun. Recurring: v1.0.778/779/782 all show `Advance vpinned marker` as the ticket-visible failed job.

**Fix approach**: widen `release-provenance`'s `if` from `needs.binaries.result == 'success'` to `needs.binaries.result != 'skipped'`. On a cancelled/failed binaries stage the job now RUNS, its gh-1832 required-assets gate fails **loudly and before any signing/publishing** (fail-closed, draft untouched — the gate precedes sign+flip), and a FAILED job is rerunnable — `rerun --failed` recovers the train. When `binaries` skips (failed quality gate / non-release refs), provenance still skips: nothing was built, nothing to sign. Pin with a workflow-shape guard test (repo convention: `ci_red_report_release_legs_guard_test.dart`, `ci_2408_rosetta_interpreter_guard_test.dart`).

**Operational recovery for v1.0.782** (independent of the code fix, which the rerun does not contain): full rerun of run 45830131519 started (attempt 2, sanctioned by docs/ci.md "a rerun keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims"). If `fa-m5-3` serves the checkout, the train publishes v1.0.782, advances the marker, and the ref goes green — the ticket's stated close condition.

### Root Cause
- The `Advance vpinned marker` red on tag v1.0.782 was a downstream symptom (run 45830131519). The self-hosted runner `fa-m5-3` hung 45 min inside the checkout `git fetch` on the `binaries-macos-x64` leg; the job's `timeout-minutes: 45` cancelled it.
- `release-provenance` (the sole publish point: signed SHA256SUMS + `--draft=false --latest` flip) then **skipped** on its `needs.binaries.result == 'success'` gate, so the v1.0.782 release stayed a draft and the vpinned marker stayed at v1.0.781 — `pin_release.sh` correctly refused (`E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING`, fail-closed by design).
- The defect this exposes: a **skipped** publish point is unreachable by `gh run rerun --failed` (repo invariant, v1.0.483), so the only recovery was a ~2h full rerun.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `release-provenance` gate widened from `needs.binaries.result == 'success'` to `needs.binaries.result != 'skipped'` — on a cancelled/failed binaries stage the job now RUNS, and its gh-1832 required-assets gate fails **loudly before** signing or the publish flip (fail-closed; the draft stays the rerun vessel). When `binaries` skips (failed quality gate / non-release refs), provenance still skips — nothing was built, nothing to sign. Mirrors the v1.0.483 `install-pin-bump` always() precedent.
- `test/ci_release_provenance_rerunnable_gate_test.dart` (new): workflow-shape guard (RED first, then GREEN) pinning rerunnability, the preserved skip arm, `!cancelled()` + tag/release gates, and downstream coherence (asset-smoke still needs success; train-draft-guard deletes only on `skipped`; install-pin-bump stays always()).
- `test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`: assertion updated to the new invariant (provenance stays keyed on the binaries result / reachable on the deduped twin).

### Test Coverage
- `ci_release_provenance_rerunnable_gate_test` — reproduction failed against the old gate (3 failed / 7 passed), passes after the fix.
- Workflow/release guard family: 199 tests passed; `ci_release_dedupe_guard_test` 25 passed; analyze + format clean; full deterministic suite: see run log.

### Notes
- Operational recovery: the tag run was fully re-run (attempt 2, sanctioned by docs/ci.md "a rerun keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims") — when `fa-m5-3` serves the checkout, v1.0.782 publishes, the marker advances, and the ref goes green (this ticket's close condition). The code fix does not ride the rerun (workflows execute from the tag ref); it makes every future incident of this class recoverable via `rerun --failed`.
- No product code touched; no secrets/config changes; no integration dependencies added.

+    # `gh run rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs (v1.0.483),
